AI Demand Continues to Surge as SK hynix Reports Record Revenue and Profit in 2Q26  SK hynix reported record-breaking results for the second quarter of FY2026, posting revenue of ₩79.318T, up 257% YoY. Operating profit reached ₩60.5426T, representing a 557% YoY increase, while net profit totaled ₩93.9226T. The company achieved an operating margin of 76% and a net margin of 118%, with both quarterly revenue and profit reaching all-time highs. Cumulative first-half revenue also exceeded ₩100T for the first time.  SK hynix attributed its strong performance to continued price increases for both DRAM and NAND Flash, alongside robust demand for high-value-added products, including HBM, AI server DRAM, and enterprise SSDs (eSSDs). As AI continues evolving toward Agentic AI and becomes increasingly integrated across a broad range of services, the company expects memory demand to broaden beyond AI-specific applications, creating a structural growth trend in both AI-oriented and mainstream memory markets.  On the DRAM front, SK hynix further strengthened its leadership in HBM. The company's HBM4, offering industry-leading power efficiency and cost competitiveness, entered mass production during the second quarter, with production scheduled to expand further in the second half of the year. Customer samples of HBM4E were also successfully delivered during the first half of 2026. Additionally, SOCAMM2, manufactured using the company's sixth-generation 10nm-class (1c) process technology, officially entered volume shipments and recorded strong sales growth during the quarter.  In the NAND Flash business, 321L QLC products have become the company's highest-volume NAND offering. SK hynix aims to increase the proportion of 321L QLC production at its Korean manufacturing facilities to approximately 50% by the end of 2026, further optimizing its product mix toward higher-performance, higher-value storage solutions.  TrendForce previously noted that major memory suppliers continue prioritizing capital expenditure toward DRAM expansion, leaving NAND Flash capacity additions relatively limited. As a result, NAND supply growth in 2026 has primarily been driven by process technology migration rather than significant capacity expansion, keeping market supply relatively tight without signs of substantial oversupply.   Looking ahead to 2027, suppliers in South Korea, the U.S., and Japan are expected to continue advancing process technologies while gradually bringing new capacity online. Meanwhile, Chinese manufacturers are projected to further expand production as additional equipment enters operation, with China's share of global NAND Flash supply expected to approach 19%. TrendForce expects the NAND Flash market to gradually rebalance in 2H27 as new capacity ramps throughout the industry, easing the current supply tightness.  📊 More semiconductor insights: https://buff.ly/4466Utg  📊 More industry charts: https://buff.ly/4hbxzLr

Intel Posts Strongest Revenue Growth in More Than 15 Years, with 2Q26 Revenue Reaching $16.1B  Intel reported 2Q26 revenue of $16.1B on July 23, representing 25% YoY growth and once again exceeding guidance. CEO Lip-Bu Tan described the quarter as Intel's strongest revenue growth in more than 15 years, highlighting that AI is driving unprecedented demand for computing. He added that Intel is well positioned to sustain long-term growth through its CPU portfolio, AI ASICs, advanced packaging technologies, and expanding foundry ecosystem.   hashtag #AIInferenceDemandDrives59PercentGrowthinDCAI Intel's Data Center and AI (DCAI) business generated $6.3B in revenue during the quarter, up 59% YoY, making it the company's fastest-growing business segment. Meanwhile, the Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) reported revenue of $8.9B, an increase of 13% YoY. The company partnered with SambaNova and Foxconn to showcase a production-ready, rack-scale infrastructure platform for Agentic AI inference. Additionally, Vector Core Compute (VC2) introduced a distributed agentic AI cloud solution integrating Intel Xeon processors, SambaNova RDUs, and NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.   hashtag #18APEntersRiskProductionasIntelExpandsCapacity Intel Foundry reported $5.8B in revenue, up 31% YoY. On the manufacturing front, Intel 18A-P entered risk production on schedule, delivering further improvements in performance, power efficiency, and thermal characteristics. Selected Core Ultra Series 3 (Panther Lake) processors have also entered volume production using ASML's High-NA EUV (EXE) lithography platform. Intel announced a €5B investment to expand manufacturing capacity, increasing output of Intel 3-based Xeon 6 and next-generation Xeon processors. The company further expanded its custom silicon portfolio through a partnership with Fortinet to develop security processors, broadening its ASIC business beyond networking and IPUs.   hashtag #3Q26RevenueGuidedtoUS16Point8B For 3Q26, Intel expects revenue of $15.8–16.8B. CFO David Zinsner said stronger-than-expected shipments were driven by higher manufacturing yields and shorter production cycles. As AI computing demand continues to accelerate, Intel plans to significantly increase investments in manufacturing equipment, cleanroom capacity, and advanced substrates to support growth across both its product portfolio and foundry business over the next two years. Operating cash flow reached $7B during the quarter.  📊 More semiconductor insights: https://buff.ly/UWCDvd1 📊 More industry charts: https://buff.ly/4hbxzLr
